<post>
Food seasoning: salt.

Food ingredients for the dog:
One piece of connective tissue and two meat scraps.
Cutting it and them.

Separately, connective tissue for the dog.
</post>

<explanation>
The first heading establishes food-seasoning purpose. The ingredient heading resolves "it" to the one tissue piece and "them" to the two meat scraps, all food ingredients for the dog. Cutting applies to each part and both together; retain the partial subjects and their complete shared action.

Each row shows the complete source collection beneath every numbered occurrence of its heading, including both Dog food branches; compatible intermediate headings may arrange the collection.

| Heading | Complete distinct source subjects collected below the heading |
| --- | --- |
| Dog-food ingredients | One piece of connective tissue as a food ingredient for the dog; Two meat scraps as food ingredients for the dog; One piece of connective tissue and two meat scraps as food ingredients for the dog; Cutting one piece of connective tissue as a food ingredient for the dog; Cutting two meat scraps as food ingredients for the dog; Cutting one piece of connective tissue and two meat scraps as food ingredients for the dog |
| One piece of connective tissue and two meat scraps as food ingredients for the dog | Cutting one piece of connective tissue and two meat scraps as food ingredients for the dog |

Either partial cutting subject omits a counted ingredient and stays outside the exact full-group heading. The full cutting subject also belongs below both partials; reverse directions lose a material or action restriction.

Salt and connective tissue can have nonfood uses. Tissue "for the dog" specifies a recipient, not a food role; it could be for a training scent. Those unrestricted headings stay outside Food and Dog food. Separate Salt, Connective tissue, Meat scraps and Dogs subjects remain alongside the actions. The separate recipient clause adds no ingredient relationship.
</explanation>
